structure: A corpus of 190 trace.zip folders (one per Playwright test run, folder names animals-e2e-... or ins-e2e-...) plus report.json (Playwright 1.63.0 JSON report, run 2026-10-07: 181 expected, 6 skipped, 0 unexpected, 2 flaky; two traces are retry1 folders). Specs live under animals/e2e/{features,features/address-book,journeys,journeys/persistence,pages,visual} and ins/e2e/features[/address-book] in the tests repo. IMPORTANT LIMIT: the prescribed trace CLI (tim distil trace -> playwright trace open) refuses every trace with 'TraceVersionError: The trace was created by a newer version of Playwright', so no snapshot, rendered DOM, action list or request log could be read through it. The only trace content read was ONE trace (ins-e2e-features-address-b-98ed4-e-address-book-landing-page-ins) unzipped by hand and read as raw JSONL (actions and network log). A bulk unzip of the other traces was denied by the permission classifier and not pursued. Everything else here comes from report.json: spec file, line and test title for every one of the ~190 runs, which states what each test proves. Scope line: every trace in the folder is in scope (whole folder, no filtering); no page copy, field labels, hints, option lists or validation message text were readable, so none is recorded and every such surface is written as a gap. Journeys and features covered by titles: animals project (sign-in/auth, dashboard list/search/sort/pagination/actions, journey entry and reference strip, hub with six numbered groups, per-page specs for origin, commodities, consignment, arrival, transporter(s), transit countries, CPH, additional details, animal identification, import reason/purpose, contact address, declaration, check-your-answers, submit/amend/cancel-amend/copy/delete lifecycle, documents upload and scan lifecycle, address-book handshake with INS and copied addresses, persistence to Mongo) and ins project (address book CRUD and organisation scoping, add-handshake guard, aggregated notification, cross-service sessions, dashboard view hand-off). Claims are ordered as the report lists them.
